title: Tuna & Corn Pasta Salad
description: A quick cold pasta salad with tuna, corn, and a light creamy dressing.
substitutions: Use canned chicken instead of tuna.

cookSteps.text: Cook 8 ounces short pasta according to the package, then drain and rinse briefly under cool water.
In a large bowl, stir 1/4 cup mayonnaise or yogurt, 1 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon mustard if using, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Add the cooled pasta, 1 drained can tuna, and 1 cup corn. Toss until evenly coated.
Serve right away or chill 15 minutes if you prefer it colder.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days in a covered container.

title: Cheesy Broccoli Toast Melts
description: Crisp toast topped with chopped broccoli and melted cheese for a fast lunch or light dinner.
equipment: sheet pan or toaster oven tray
substitutions: Use any good melting cheese you have.

steps.text: Heat the broiler and toast the bread lightly.

cookSteps.text: Heat the broiler. Put 4 bread slices on a sheet pan and toast lightly if the bread is very soft.
Mix 1 1/2 cups chopped cooked broccoli with 2 tablespoons mayonnaise or yogurt if using and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder.
Divide the broccoli over the toast and top with 1 cup shredded cheddar.
Broil 2–4 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftover topping up to 3 days and assemble fresh toast when ready.

title: Tomato Cabbage Rice Soup
description: A simple, filling soup that turns cabbage, canned tomatoes, and rice into an inexpensive meal.
substitutions: Use leftover cooked rice; stir in 1 1/2 cups during the final 5 minutes instead.
Add white beans for extra protein.

steps.text: Simmer until the rice and cabbage are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 4 cups chopped cabbage, 1 can diced tomatoes, 1/2 cup uncooked rice, 6 cups broth, 1 diced small onion, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cover loosely and simmer 25–30 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice and cabbage are tender.
Taste and add salt if needed before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. The rice absorbs broth as it sits; add extra broth or water when reheating.

title: No-Bake Cocoa Oat Squares
description: Soft chocolatey oat squares made on the stovetop with pantry basics and no oven.
substitutions: Use quick oats for a softer texture.

steps.text: Stir in oats and chill until firm.

cookSteps.text: Line a loaf pan or small food-storage container with parchment or lightly grease it.
Combine 1/4 cup butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup milk, and 2 tablespoons cocoa in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Stir until smooth and gently bubbling, then cook 1 minute.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using and 1 1/2 cups rolled oats.
Press firmly into the prepared pan and refrigerate about 30 minutes until set.

storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days in a covered container.
